root_cause.text: In __smc_setsockopt(), the copy_from_sockptr() call is executed while holding lock_sock(sk), allowing a local attacker to block indefinitely on userfaultfd-monitored memory, causing a sleep-inside-lock that holds the socket lock and leads to a denial of service via hung workqueues.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves the copy_from_sockptr() for SMC_LIMIT_HS outside the lock_sock() critical section. The commit description explicitly states the flaw: "The function __smc_setsockopt() calls copy_from_sockptr() while holding lock_sock(sk). By passing a userfaultfd-monitored memory page ... an attacker can halt execution during the copy operation, keeping the lock held."
